Chapter 10: Living as a Bridge—Carrying the Past into the Present
Picture this. In those quiet moments at the very end of her journey, she paused to reflect on everything she’d learned along the way. She saw herself as a bridge—someone who carried the stories of the past right into the present, connecting generations through memory and love.
Of course, it wasn’t always easy. There were days when the weight of history felt almost too heavy to carry, when old pain threatened to pull her under. Maybe you’ve felt that way too—like the past is pressing down, more than you bargained for.
But then, there were moments of pure grace. Little flashes—her child’s laughter, her mother’s warm smile, her community coming together to remember and, somehow, to heal. In those times, she realized she wasn’t alone at all. She was part of something so much bigger than herself.
That’s when it hit her: being a bridge is both a responsibility and a gift. It means facing the truth, even when it hurts. It means making room for both grief and joy, for sorrow and hope. And, maybe most importantly, it’s about believing in healing—even when the wounds run deep.
Most people go through life without really reckoning with the stories they inherit. But for her, the journey became a way to claim her place in the world. To honor those who came before her. And to offer something better to the ones who would come after.
